text:
Zoe: Customer (StripePros) reporting 504s and many client timeouts since ~09:12 PST. They say p95 jumped to ~30s and some requests never returned. They provided a couple request IDs: req_01e, req_01f.
Maya: ACK — opening here and pinging oncall. Any obvious alerts?
InfraBot: Alert: hosted-gateway.request_queue_depth > 0.95 for pool: hosted-prod-us-west-2 (09:14). Rolling average queue_depth 98%.
Raj: Seeing the same in dashboards — continuous-batcher backlog spiking, KV-cache miss rate up. Many requests stuck waiting to be batched.
Lin: Do we have recent deploys to batcher or kernel that could change batch sizing? Not on the deployment timeline. Last infra deploy was 02:00 UTC.
Owen: Oncall here. I'm collecting traces and will run a repro against staging routing to same model variant.
Maya: Customer says this started after a traffic spike — they had a burst of long-context requests (~10k tokens) to a hosted endpoint.
Raj: Long sequences will increase per-token service time and reduce throughput. If continuous batching keeps accumulating long requests, tail latency will shoot.
Zoe: They also noted a few 401s earlier but those look unrelated — API key rotation event maybe. Main problem is request backlog.
Lin: Quick check: current batcher config for that pool: `max_batch_bytes: 6e6`, `max_batch_latency_ms: 25`, `max_concurrent_requests: 200`, `queue_depth_limit: 1000` — but observed per-worker in-flight ~= 950 queued.
Raj: From traces: many requests sit in queue for 18-28s before dequeue. Service time once dequeued is ~300-800ms. So tail is queuing not compute.
Owen: Immediate mitigation: enable prefix eviction and reduce `max_batch_latency_ms` to 10ms for the affected pool, and temporarily lower `max_batch_bytes` to reduce aggregation of long requests. Propose running a rolling restart of batch workers with the new config.
Maya: I'll propose the config change to the CS contact and ask for permission to perform a brief rolling restart. If they consent, we can do a staged rollout.
Lin: Also suggest enabling adaptive shedding for very long-context requests — cap seq_len per-request to 8192 for hosted tier or route to dedicated if they need 10k+ tokens.
Zoe: Customer approved emergency changes.
Raj: Executing quick change: `curl -X POST https://controlplane.internal/pools/hosted-prod-us-west-2/config -d '{"max_batch_latency_ms":10,"max_batch_bytes":3000000}'` -> 202 accepted.
InfraBot: Config change applied to 3/5 batcher pods. Initiating rolling restart of batcher pods (pods 2-5) with zero-downtime drain.
Owen: Watching metrics... queue_depth drops from 98% -> 60% within 45s. p95 tail drops from 30s -> ~6.2s. Some 504s still trickling.
Raj: Good improvement. Next step: backfill KV-cache hotspots — there are many cache misses for prefix keys 0xdeadbeef. Trigger cache warm for top customers and enable short-lived prefix cache TTL extension.
Lin: Running cache warm command: `./kvcache-warm --pool hosted-prod-us-west-2 --keys-file hot_keys.txt`.
Maya: Customer reports degraded but improving experience, 504 rate down 80%. They're asking for a postmortem and longer-term mitigation.
Zoe: Noted. Action items: 1) Postmortem with traffic shape and root cause. 2) Recommend routing policy to off-ramp long-context requests to a dedicated queue. 3) Consider lowering queue_depth_limit or implement graceful shed on threshold. 4) Add alerting refinement to catch sustained queue_depth > 0.85 for >1m.
Raj: I'll draft the postmortem and include traces + the exact config diffs.
Lin: Also scheduling a small infra change: adaptive batcher that weights by expected seq_len and rejects or re-routes extremely long requests before full queue saturation.
Owen: Marking this incident as mitigated for now — continuing to monitor for 2 hours.
Maya: Logged the customer escalation ticket and cc'd support and CS.
Zoe: Thanks team. We'll follow up with the customer with a timeline for the fixes. :thumbsup:
